newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank to offer price guarantee on Telekom stock.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank to offer price guarantee on Telekom stock.

text.p: Commerzbank AG is to offer private investors a price guarantee on shares in soon-to-be floated telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom -- the latest bid to lure risk-averse Germans to the stock market.

The bank will hold Telekom shares on deposit for clients from their time of issue until after Telekom's shareholder meeting in 2002, with a guaranteed return of the initial investment plus any gains accrued in the stock price.
Investors will, however, lose all dividends and tax credits paid out in the period, since these will be absorbed by Commerzbank to cover its costs.
Launching the first-of-its-kind offer, called Safe-T, on Wednesday, Commerzbank board member Peter Gloystein said the programme was geared to the needs of the vast majority of German investors.

"We eliminate investors' worries about share price decreases, let them fully participate in price increases and we keep the dividends, which for many investors are less important than the potential rise in price," Gloystein said.

Investors can opt out of the deposit programme at any time, and will receive a price close to the current stock market level, minus "appropriate" deductions, depending on whether a dividend payment is imminent for example.
The ultimate aim, Gloystein said, is that participants will be sufficiently confident by 2002 to hold on to their Telekom shares as a direct investment.
The Telekom flotation, whose first tranche is expected to go ahead in November, will be Germany's biggest ever and is viewed as a test for the nation's fledgling equity culture.

Telekom says around 1.8 million individuals have expressed interest in buying its stock and is to offer private investors discounts of one to five percent off the initial share price -- an offer which will also apply to Commerzbank's programme.
Banks have leapt firmly on the bandwagon, with all the major players already offering high-interest paying special savings schemes in advance of the Telekom launch.
"The banks here are all up against each other in this competition," said Commerzbank's Gloystein.

Commerzbank said a survey had shown that a quarter of Germans who do not yet own shares -- about 90 percent of the population -- would be prepared to do so if the risk element attached to equities were removed.

The bank is launching its biggest ever marketing campaign for Safe-T, with promotional letters to be sent to 1.4 million non-customers and 900,000 existing customers and advertisements to run on all media and hopes to attract around 15,000 new clients through the offer.
Commerzbank said 9,000 clients were already in its Telekom savings scheme and had amassed 150 million marks ($99.08 million).
